source.title: Efficiency Matters in Autonomous Research
source.publication_status: ARXIV_PREPRINT_V1; no peer-reviewed venue established by the supplied full text

source.extraction_scope: ORX paper --full extracted text; figures read through text/captions, PDF pixels not independently inspected.

claims.claim: The study distinguishes final outcome from search efficiency and defines frontier R(n) as archive-best verified reward, with AUC the average frontier reward over evaluation count.

Controlled comparison uses 12 AutoLab systems-optimization tasks, Qwen3-Coder-480B FP8 single-completion proposer without a multi-turn agentic loop, four fixed policies, width64, 500 evaluations and three seeds per task.

Greedy divides trials among independent incumbent chains; beam concentrates on selected frontier candidates; tree allocates among branches; evolutionary search maintains a population with tournament parent selection.

Fluid allocates the next evaluation to an idle hill-climbing chain using recent incumbent improvement, current quality and UCB-style exploration. It is not a demonstrated heterogeneous portfolio of search algorithms.
The fluid package additionally uses archival reseeding, stalled/crashing-chain restart, bounded edits of crashed artifacts, persistent duplicate softening and a 16-to-64 chain warm start.
Author-reported normalized AUC is fluid0.780, beam0.718, and per-task oracle0.784. The ceiling and best-policy oracle use observed outcomes from these same evaluated tasks/runs.
claims.numeric_scope: External author-reported within-suite metric only; no local or B/C/G efficacy or power prior.

claims.claim: Paper explicitly limits evidence to fixed representation and fixed, inexpensive, formal, immediate verifier; delayed downstream usefulness and adaptive verification are beyond the evaluated scope.
The read text describes switchable mechanisms but does not report independent ablation results for every fluid lever; do not attribute the total gain to the bandit, archive or warm start alone.
claims.negative_evidence_scope: Full source read1-1061; no additional code or supplement inspected.

claims.claim: A search tree or forest here is candidate-state search allocation, not a versioned scholarly evidence/dependency graph. This paper does not directly show graph-grounding efficacy or long-horizon source recovery.

comparability_limits: Evaluation count is their cost unit, not measured total tokens, money, CPU/GPU, human work or wall time for the local programme.
The paper motivates expensive physical verification while its actual verifier is inexpensive, fixed, formal and immediate.
Its running archive-best reward and observed task ceiling differ from the current single preselected final-artifact MAE endpoint.
Concurrent32 jobs over64 chains, warm start8 jobs over16 chains and500 trials do not transfer to the current P0 3 dev/1 final-refit protocol.
No local replication, full raw trace/code audit, publication-venue check or independent statistical verification occurred in this lane.
Three seeds per task and twelve systems tasks are external study design choices, not local independent efficacy units or sample-size justification.
The paper does not study B/C/G compulsory research gates, source-version changes, hidden evaluation custody or cross-context evidence validity.
Crash repair in this verifier-controlled search cannot justify retrying ambiguous external scientific runs or resetting consumed local authority.

design_proposals.proposal: Keep search-budget allocation as a separate design axis from evidence-state representation. For an interpretable B/C/G comparison, share the scheduler and its trial rights across arms; a later scheduler/representation package comparison must be named as such.

Retain the existing one-locked-artifact hidden MAE endpoint. Add only a prespecified development anytime curve and complete actual-cost accounting as complementary measures. Never obtain repeated hidden scores to build an archive-best curve.

Use greedy/beam/tree/population/adaptive allocation as mechanism-distinct internal design alternatives without adding all as mandatory experimental arms. The paper challenges selecting one topology by intuition but does not pick the winner for House Price.

Treat completed experiment records as scheduler observations and retain one scientific-run owner. The evidence graph can record dependency applicability separately from quality/progress used for allocation; graph size alone is not a budget-allocation reward.

manuscript_boundary: Scholarly source may inform a qualified related-work/method claim only with preprint status retained. No tool branding, implementation existence or local efficacy is established. Manuscript writing remains subject to existing ResearchDone boundary.
decision: Use as directly supported evidence that search allocation and anytime efficiency deserve a separate design axis. It neither selects the graph mechanism nor replaces the locked-artifact primary endpoint.
